text: So, sign language names aren't just an arbitrary translation of your spoken name. They're more like a monosyllabic nickname, something short and easy to sign. People usually come up with them, or friends give them to you. They're based on your character traits, your physical appearance, or a nickname you're commonly known by. So a person who's very tall might get the sign for tall. Or there's someone who's very fast, he gets the sign for fast. It's just a sign that you're recognizable by. And some people are more comfortable with having a sign language name that's not based on their actual name. There's also a thing called a borrowed name, which is a sign that's used as your name, but it's not actually your name. But a lot of people will just borrow the sign for their spoken name if the letters of the spoken name have an initial-finger spelling.
